headline: South Asia: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy reports four Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's Pivnichnyi Bridge.
- Asia: Trump confirms fresh Iran strikes days after voters punish war at polls.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 20 hours ago: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
With tensions in Jamaica’s Parliament escalating this week, a government lecturer is calling for tougher sanctions against lawmakers who breach parliamentary procedures, warning that failure to act could see the House of Representatives degenerate into a “brawl”.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 20 hours ago: Privy Council shuts door on Dawkins Brown’s fight to regain accountant’s licence.
The United Kingdom-based Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has refused Dawkins Brown permission to appeal his removal from Jamaica’s Register of Public Accountants, bringing his latest attempt to overturn the disciplinary decision to an end. The refusal, handed down last month, means Brown has failed to secure a hearing before Jamaica’s highest appellate court in his battle against the Public Accountancy Board (PAB), which struck him off the professional register in March 2020 and ordered him to pay $1.6 million towards the costs of its disciplinary proceedings.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 20 hours ago: Why achieving your goals can leave you feeling so empty.
THE CONVERSATION: When Anne Carson learned she had won the Nobel Prize in literature, she was in Iceland, where, according to the Swedish Academy, she was "listening to the wind". Carson didn't answer her phone right away, silencing it until her husband persuaded her to call back. Her verdict on the academy's choice: "I think you're all insane." Whatever she felt in the moment, there is an irony in Carson's Nobel win. The highest award in literature has gone to a writer who has spent her career exploring the emptiness of a desire fulfilled.

- Military Times, one day ago: How Afghanistan War soul-searching led to renaming of Navy expeditionary command.
The command's recent name change was years in the making after the end of the Afghanistan War, according to the head of Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
A hysterical map on social media has cooked up an image of the blast radius of radioactive fallout if Iran’s nuclear facilities were attacked. It fancies that it shows how radiation would reach Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, parts of Afghanistan, and potentially other areas depending on atmospheric conditions.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot to try to form government.
Israel’s president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an Oct 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he would have a majority of seats in parliament.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Taipei Times, 2 hours ago: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war.
Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme. Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, one hour ago: Poland says 6 killed in shooting in central Krakow.
Poland’s police said on Saturday that six people were killed and around a dozen wounded after a gunman opened fire in the historic centre of its second city, Krakow. A man drove a car onto Krakow’s Main Square and began shooting at random people, said police. Officers shot a suspect who is now in custody, they added. “As a result of the incident, five people were killed and around a dozen others were wounded,” a Krakow police spokesman told AFP by phone. “The perpetrator was shot by police” and was transported to a hospital, regional police said on X.

His death was later confirmed by the ⁠National Unity of Hope party, or UNE, to which he ‌belonged. Arevalo said the three...

Washington is offering a US$20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme, the US military has said, as President Donald Trump reiterated that Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to US$20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear programme, including its facilities, equipment and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific...

Myanmar’s military-backed government may find its reluctance to address the international community’s concerns a greater obstacle to economic recovery than the threat of tougher international financial restrictions, according to analysts. - NDTV - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: AAP Invokes 1984 Riots In Attack On Rahul Gandhi After His 'Drinking' Jab At Bhagwant Mann.
What started as a personal exchange over alcohol consumption and the drug menace has now expanded into a confrontation involving Sikh identity, the 1984 anti-Sikh violence, and the Congress's political legacy.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: From Rs 50,000 pickle startup to national award: Kerala woman's spice success.
Bindulekha S faced financial struggles after her garment business collapsed due to Covid-19. She borrowed Rs 50,000 and started making pickles, quickly gaining popularity and expanding her product range. Support from organizations helped her improve food-processing techniques and marketing strategies. Bindulekha's venture, Shri Krishna Pickles, now includes several women and a roadside eatery. Her business recently earned national recognition for its quality and variety at a major food fair.

- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne to remain in public hands after partial backtrack on defence property selloff.
Four heritage-listed defence properties to be preserved for community use after backlash from veterans and former PMs Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Four heritage-listed defence sites, including Sydney’s Victoria Barracks, will remain in public hands after the Albanese government yielded to public backlash against their sale. The sites, along with 63 others around the country, were identified in an independent audit as being underutilised by defence, not fit for purpose and costly to maintain, and were earmarked for sale to recoup $3bn in the federal budget.
